source.title: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models

confidence_rationale: GPT-3 solves a broad range of zero-shot analogy problems (matrix reasoning, letter-string, verbal analogies) with no dedicated analogy operator and no analogy-specific training -- direct support for the 'analogy emerges from a general relational substrate' horn. Discounted heavily because (a) whether the LLM's behaviour is genuine relational analogy or surface pattern-completion is actively contested (Hodel & West counterexamples on trivially-perturbed letter-string tasks), and (b) an LLM's substrate is not MECH-300 cognitive-map traversal, so the mapping is 'a general model can do analogy without a special module', not a demonstration about REE's specific traversal mechanism.
failure_signatures: GPT-3 has been shown to fail simple variations of the same letter-string analogies that humans solve robustly, suggesting some of the apparent analogy is brittle pattern-matching rather than structure alignment -- if REE's emergence were similarly brittle it would fail the very generalization analogy is supposed to buy.

Emergence in a trillion-token language model does not establish emergence in a compact symbolic-map substrate; the result may be parasitic on scale and training distribution rather than on relational-map traversal per se.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Large language models (GPT-3/GPT-4), without any analogy-specific training, acquire an emergent zero-shot capacity to solve a wide range of analogy problems, in several cases matching or exceeding human performance.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-074's emergence horn says analogy need not be a hand-built operator -- it can fall out of a sufficiently rich general substrate. Webb et al. is the strongest behavioural instance of that pattern in an artificial system: a general next-token predictor exhibits analogical reasoning it was never explicitly given. By analogy to REE, if a general relational-inference stack (MECH-419/MECH-420) is rich enough, MECH-421 might not need to be a separate module.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The substrate is wrong twice over: an LLM is not MECH-300 cognitive-map traversal, and 'emergence at scale in a language model' may not predict 'emergence from a compact symbolic map'. Whether the LLM behaviour is genuine analogy is itself disputed, so this supports the emergence hypothesis only weakly and provisionally.
mapping.source_context: Behavioural comparison of GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) against human participants on non-visual matrix reasoning (Raven-style), letter-string analogies, four-term verbal analogies, and story analogies.

confidence_components.notes: Venue and human-comparison design are strong (source_quality 0.80), but the contested-genuineness debate and the double substrate mismatch pull mapping_fidelity and transfer_risk toward the middle; net moderate support for the emergence horn.
